Cultivator — Read This First

Executive Summary: What Changed, What We Are Building, What Must Be Proven

The pitch is no longer “a cheap aerator sensor.” It is a closed-loop oxygen assurance system linking pond need to verified aerator response.

The pond should wake the aerator.
Not the farmer.

Cultivator uses dissolved oxygen + current sensing to decide when aeration is needed, control it safely, verify the aerator actually responded, and reduce unnecessary motor-hours without weakening oxygen safety.

Real farm · Indonesia · 05:10

1. What changed

  • Vibration removed: focus = current + DO.
  • Monitoring → closed-loop control.
  • Value = risk + energy + labor reduction.
  • NT$1,000 sensor anchor → value-based system pricing.
  • HydroNeo = market validation, not a straw-man competitor.

2. New commercial model

  • Pond Core + optical DO: NT$24,900.
  • Aerator Node: NT$6,900/aerator.
  • 6-aerator example: NT$66,300 hardware.
  • Pro: NT$1,490/pond/month.
  • Monitoring → control → Fleet / enterprise.
  • Smallholder option: financing / pay-from-savings.

3. What needs attention

  • Prove energy savings. No 15–30% claim yet.
  • Confirm DO-control BOM + ~NT$3,000 node COGS.
  • Measure full-system installation time.
  • Prepare proof for pilots + Maxmar claims.
  • Rebuild SAM bottom-up.
  • Add warranty, service, inventory and channel costs.

Commercial strategy

Why NT$1,000 was the wrong anchor.

Old product

Current monitor

The NT$1,000 price treated Cultivator like a commodity sensor. That can work as a penetration product but does not reflect closed-loop DO control.

New product

Oxygen assurance system

Pond-level DO state + local safety control + per-aerator current sensing + actuation verification + cloud intelligence.

Smallholder affordability

Two ways to buy the same outcome.

Ownership

NT$66,300 + NT$1,490/month

Best for larger operators and farms that prefer capital purchase. Local safety control remains on-device; Pro pays for remote data, analytics and AI features.

Financed service

NT$9,900 setup + NT$2,290/month × 36

Total contract value ≈ NT$92,340. Designed so monthly payment can sit below verified savings once the field trial proves the economics.

Do not lock safety behind SaaS. If cloud service is not renewed, critical local DO control should continue. This follows a trust-building principle already used by HydroNeo.
Enterprise pilot model

For Maxmar: align price with proof.

New Cultivator principleShow product cost only after the judge understands the recurring value.
Financial storytelling comparison

Use RenaiSun's discipline, not its exact model.

Past Cultivator: operating forecast mixes pilots, active products, MRR and cost assumptions with inconsistent units.
RenaiSun: revenue, funding, units, operating profit, ROI and break-even are separated into a staged roadmap.
Apply

Make units explicit, separate revenue types, label targets vs actuals, and show what unlocks the next stage.

Do not copy blindly

Cultivator is hardware + recurring software, so MRR and installed-base economics matter more than one-time unit sales alone.

Slide 01 · analytical comparison + script

The pond should wake the aerator. Not the farmer.

Comparison

Past Cultivator decks opened with global-market scale or 'Farming Without Uncertainty.' RenaiSun immediately names the product and outcome. This opening keeps that clarity but adds a human operating moment.

Design rule

Visible slide stays sparse: one headline, one core visual, and only the numbers the judge must remember. Assumptions stay in the report appendix.

Predicted script · ~20-30 seconds

Shrimp farms depend on aerators every hour of the day, but farmers still spend nights checking whether the machines are running and whether the pond has enough oxygen. Cultivator connects pond need to machine response, so the system can react before the farmer has to.

Slide 02 · analytical comparison + script

2-3 AM checks are a symptom.

Comparison

Past problem slides stacked fragility, crop loss, bankruptcy and 2-3 AM checks. RenaiSun separates traditional-process pains across multiple pages. This page keeps only the night-check behavior.

Design rule

Visible slide stays sparse: one headline, one core visual, and only the numbers the judge must remember. Assumptions stay in the report appendix.

Predicted script · ~20-30 seconds

The night check is not the root problem. It is a workaround. Farmers wake up because they cannot continuously trust oxygen conditions or aerator operation. If we only add another dashboard, we digitize the same anxiety.

Slide 03 · analytical comparison + script

The timer knows the clock. It does not know the pond.

Comparison

Past pitches did not clearly visualize the incumbent control logic. RenaiSun explicitly shows traditional drying before the innovation.

Design rule

Visible slide stays sparse: one headline, one core visual, and only the numbers the judge must remember. Assumptions stay in the report appendix.

Predicted script · ~20-30 seconds

This is the control logic many farms already use: schedules and manual judgment. It is simple, but blind. It cannot see where oxygen is heading, and it cannot verify the aerator is behaving normally.

Slide 04 · analytical comparison + script

Farmers buy safety with electricity.

Comparison

Older decks focused on catastrophic failure. The newer strategy recognizes energy as a recurring measurable pain. RenaiSun converts technical innovation into lower operating cost early.

Design rule

Visible slide stays sparse: one headline, one core visual, and only the numbers the judge must remember. Assumptions stay in the report appendix.

Predicted script · ~20-30 seconds

Without confidence about oxygen, the rational response is to run more aerators for longer. That buys safety, but with electricity. Cultivator's control objective is simple: minimum aeration while maintaining a hard oxygen safety margin.

Slide 05 · analytical comparison + script

Sense. Predict. Act. Verify.

Comparison

Past decks spread hardware, dashboard, AI and pond health across several conceptual pages. This compresses the logic into one memorable closed loop.

Design rule

Visible slide stays sparse: one headline, one core visual, and only the numbers the judge must remember. Assumptions stay in the report appendix.

Predicted script · ~20-30 seconds

We sense DO and current, predict oxygen risk, act on the necessary aerators, then verify that the current response is normal. The important word is verify: an ON command is not success until the machine response confirms it.

Our first product is deliberately narrow: fast current monitoring per aerator. It gives on/off state, RMS current, runtime and electrical anomaly alerts. We paused vibration because current gives us a simpler, cheaper and more deployable first product.
